module purpose: neorv32_cpu_frontend controls instruction fetching with a fetch FSM and two prefetch-buffer lanes: it drives instruction-bus requests from a stored PC and privilege context, captures acknowledged bus responses into the buffers, optionally decompresses 16-bit instructions when RVC_EN, and outputs instruction issue information plus a halted indication on frontend_o.

use-case flows.value: load a new fetch context from ctrl_i.pc_nxt and ctrl_i.cpu_priv, clear pending restart, and enter request state
drive an instruction-bus request from the stored fetch PC and request attributes when the prefetch buffer is free
pack acknowledged instruction-bus response halves with the error bit and write them into the two prefetch-buffer lanes
when RVC_EN, select or decompress a 16-bit instruction or assemble a 32-bit instruction, report valid/compr/fault, and generate buffer read commands
when not RVC_EN, issue a 32-bit instruction from the two prefetch lanes and report valid/compr/fault
frontend_o.halted when a request is pending but both prefetch lanes are not free
reset fetch control, fetch address/privilege, and issue alignment to defined defaults while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.reasoning: Start/restart loads `fetch.pc <= ctrl_i.pc_nxt` (line 114), an acknowledged pending fetch advances it by 4 and clears bit 1 (lines 101-103), and the request flow derives `ibus_req_o.addr` from it (line 123). Integrity is established because both the request address (line 123) and the lane-0 write-enable condition that uses `fetch.pc(1)` (line 141) become incorrect if this state is corrupted. Availability is also established because the register holds the address between updates and resets to a defined value at line 84.

Restart captures `ctrl_i.cpu_priv` into `fetch.priv` at line 115 and the request flow copies it to `ibus_req_o.priv` at line 129. Integrity is established because the request consumer must receive the privilege attribute defined by the restart context; availability is established because the bit is stored until the next restart or reset (lines 85 and 115).

conceptual assets.concept: Fetch control state and pending restart decision
conceptual assets.reasoning: `fetch.restart` latches itself or `ctrl_i.if_reset` in request and pending states (lines 91 and 100) and is cleared in the restart branch (line 113); `fetch.state` moves between `S_REQUEST`, `S_PENDING`, and `S_RESTART` at lines 93, 95, 105, 107, and 116. These values control request strobing (line 124), prefetch writes (lines 141-142), halted reporting (line 145), FIFO clear through `clear_i` (line 164), and alignment reload on restart (lines 205-206). Integrity is established because corrupt control state mis-sequences fetch, flush, and issue behavior; availability is established by the held registers and reset defaults at lines 82-83.

conceptual assets.concept: Instruction-halfword alignment state used for issuing from the prefetch buffer
conceptual assets.reasoning: When `RVC_EN`, `issue.algn` is reset to `'0'` (line 203), reloaded from `ctrl_i.pc_nxt(1)` on restart (lines 205-206), and otherwise updated on `ctrl_i.if_ack` by `(issue.algn and (not issue.aclr)) or issue.aset` (lines 207-208). The issue logic uses this state at line 195 and lines 219-247 to select which prefetch lane supplies the instruction and fault bit. Integrity is established because a wrong alignment state selects the wrong halfword(s) and consume path. With `not RVC_EN`, the signal is tied to `'0'` at line 261.

When `RVC_EN`, `issue.ack` is computed as `"01"`, `"10"`, or `"11"` from the selected halfword pattern and alignment (lines 223, 228, 238, 243), and `ipb.re` combines that decision with `ctrl_i.if_ack` at lines 252-253; with `not RVC_EN`, line 266 consumes both lanes on `ctrl_i.if_ack`. Integrity is established because these commands determine which prefetched halfword(s) are removed and therefore whether the instruction stream advances correctly. Availability is established under the implemented condition that the downstream side acknowledges the issued instruction.

conceptual assets.concept: Issued instruction word delivered to the backend
conceptual assets.reasoning: Bus response halves are packed into `ipb.wdata` (lines 137-138), written into the prefetch FIFOs (lines 168-169), read back as `ipb.rdata` (line 173), and then either decompressed through `issue.cmd16`/`issue.cmd32` (lines 190-191, 195, 225, 240) or concatenated directly (lines 230, 245, 268) onto `frontend_o.instr`. Integrity is established because the backend must receive exactly the instruction word defined by these assembly rules. Availability is established conditionally when the corresponding valid conditions hold at lines 224, 229, 239, 244, and 267.

`frontend_o.valid` is driven from buffer-availability conditions: one-lane availability for compressed issue (lines 224 and 239), both lanes for 32-bit assembly (lines 229 and 244), and lane 0 when `not RVC_EN` (line 267). Integrity is established because the consumer must know whether the concurrently driven instruction output is meaningful under the implemented issue conditions.

Under `RVC_EN`, the selected halfword's low bits decide whether the frontend reports a compressed instruction (`frontend_o.compr <= '1'` at lines 226 or 241 after tests at lines 221 or 236) or a 32-bit instruction (`'0'` at lines 231 or 246); with `not RVC_EN`, line 269 fixes `'0'`. Integrity is established because this output must match the instruction-formation path actually taken.

The bus error bit is packed together with each 16-bit response halfword in `ipb.wdata` at lines 137-138, later returned on `ipb.rdata` (line 173), and selected to `frontend_o.fault` from lane 0 or lane 1 at lines 220, 235, and 270. Integrity is established because the consumer must receive the fault tag that corresponds to the issued instruction source.

`frontend_o.halted` is asserted only when `fetch.state = S_REQUEST` and `ipb.free /= "11"` (line 145). Integrity is established because this reported decision reflects the implemented stall condition that a new request is ready but the prefetch lanes are not both free.
